cohort: The study included 114 cases of canine abortion, stillbirth, and neonatal mortality, along with four fetal membranes from dystocic dams, occurring in Central Italy.
finding: Mycoplasma DNA was detected in 6.14% of the cases and one fetal membrane, often in association with other major pathogens, suggesting it may play a secondary role in canine abortion and neonatal mortality or be part of the normal genital microflora.
mod_finding: Mycoplasma DNA was detected in fetal membranes collected during a cesarean section of a bitch whose puppies tested negative for Mycoplasma.
